newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC chief says TV liquor ad ban not certain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC chief says TV liquor ad ban not certain.

text.p: The top U.S. communications regulator said on Sunday he favored barring television stations from running hard-liquor ads but conceded he would have to get some colleagues to agree to such rules.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt again called on TV broadcasters to adhere to a voluntary ban on advertisements for hard liquor, noting that the four major networks have said they would abide by the ban.
Asked whether he favored the FCC writing formal rules to enforce a ban if TV stations declined to go along, Hundt said: "We should. We ought to."

But Hundt declined on "John McLaughlin's One on One" show on NBC to predict the FCC would in fact impose such regulations, noting that he would have to convince some of the agency's four existing commissioners to go along.
Commissioners James Quello and Rachelle Chong have voiced doubts about the FCC's powers to write such rules, with Quello insisting that it is up to Congress to pass a law to bar broadcast liquor ads.

Seagram Co earlier this year broke the liquor industry's decades-old ban on broadcast ads by airing spots for its Royal Crown Whiskey. The nation's distillers followed suit earlier this autumn and lifted the ban, noting that the beer and wine industries enjoyed a competitive advantage because of their ability to run TV ads.
